title: Book search by title or author

tests.title: Partial title match
tests.what: A reader types part of a title, such as 'ring', and gets the book whose title contains it.
tests.expected: GET /books/search?q=ring returns 200 and an HTML fragment with a card for 'The Lord of the Rings'. Books whose title and author do not contain 'ring' are absent.

tests.title: Partial author match
tests.what: A reader types part of an author name, such as 'tolk', and gets that author's books.
tests.expected: GET /books/search?q=tolk returns 200 with cards for books by J.R.R. Tolkien. Books by other authors are absent.

tests.title: Case-insensitive match
tests.what: The same word typed in upper, lower and mixed case finds the same book.
tests.expected: q=DUNE, q=dune and q=DuNe all return 200 with the same set of cards, including 'Dune'.

tests.title: Accented letters case-insensitive
tests.what: A reader searches for an author with an accented capital letter.
tests.expected: q=MIÉVILLE and q=miéville (URL-encoded) both return a card for a book by China Miéville. q=Mieville (no accent) returns no card for that author.

tests.title: Title or author, whole query
tests.what: The whole query must be inside the title or inside the author. Two words split across both fields do not match.
tests.expected: q=Dune%20Herbert returns 200 and no book cards. q=Dune and q=Herbert each return 'Dune'. A book that matches in both fields appears exactly once.

tests.title: No match message
tests.what: A reader searches for text that is in no title or author.
tests.expected: Returns 200 (not an error), an HTML fragment with no book cards, and the text 'No books found'.

tests.title: Card layout and order
tests.what: Matching books are shown as on the home page and sorted by title.
tests.expected: A query matching several books returns an HTML fragment (not a full page, not JSON). Each card has the title linking to /books/<id>, 'by <author>', and the published year when present. Cards are in ascending title order. The test does not rely on the order of identical titles.

tests.title: Percent and underscore literal
tests.what: A reader types '%' or '_', which must be treated as plain characters and not as wildcards.
tests.expected: q=%25 returns 200 and no seed books ('No books found'). q=_ returns only books whose title or author literally contains an underscore (none in the seed data), not every book.

tests.title: Empty query returns all
tests.what: The reader clears the search box and sees the full list again.
tests.expected: q= (empty) returns 200 with all 50 seed books in title order ('1984' first). A non-empty query such as q=dune returns fewer cards than this full list.

tests.title: Missing or blank query
tests.what: A request with no q, or with only spaces, is treated as an empty query.
tests.expected: GET /books/search with no q, and q=%20%20%20, both return 200 with the same 50 books in the same order as q=.

tests.title: Padded query is trimmed
tests.what: A reader types a word with leading and trailing spaces.
tests.expected: q=%20%20dune%20%20 returns 200 and the same cards as q=dune. Spaces inside a query are kept: q=lord%20of matches 'The Lord of the Rings'.

tests.title: Exactly 100 characters accepted
tests.what: A query of exactly 100 characters is at the limit and is allowed.
tests.expected: A 100-letter q returns 200 (an HTML fragment, 'No books found'), not 400.

tests.title: 101 characters rejected
tests.what: A reader pastes a query that is one character over the limit.
tests.expected:
A 101-letter q returns 400 with an HTML fragment containing

with exactly 'Search query must be 100 characters or fewer'. The body has no book cards and does not repeat the submitted text.

tests.title: Limit measured after trim
tests.what: Surrounding spaces do not count toward the 100-character limit, and spaces do not hide an over-long query.
tests.expected: 100 letters wrapped in spaces (for example 5 on each side) return 200. 101 letters wrapped in spaces return 400 with the length message.

tests.title: Limit counts characters
tests.what: A query of 100 accented or non-ASCII characters is within the limit, and 101 is over.
tests.expected: 100 characters such as 'é' (200 bytes) return 200. 101 such characters return 400 with the length message.

tests.title: Repeated or nested q rejected
tests.what: A request that supplies q more than once, or as an object, is refused.
tests.expected:
?q=a&q=b and ?q[x]=a each return 400 with

containing exactly 'Search query must be a single text value'.

tests.title: Quote text is plain text
tests.what: A reader searches for an apostrophe, and a hostile user sends SQL fragments.
tests.expected: q=' returns 200 with 'Ender's Game' and 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy' (titles HTML-escaped). q=' OR 1=1 -- returns 200 with no cards, not the full list. Neither request returns an error.

tests.title: Drop-table text changes nothing
tests.what: A query that tries to drop a table is treated as text and the data stays intact.
tests.expected: q="; DROP TABLE books; -- returns 200 with 'No books found'. A following q= returns all 50 books.

coverage.note: Met by the whole set: every criterion AC-01 to AC-05 has at least one test.
Met by the whole set: the full suite, including these tests, must pass with npm run test:run.

assumptions.what: Assumes accented letters fold case and are not accent-insensitive (GAP-10). It also assumes the seed data has an author 'China Miéville'.
Assumes '%' and '_' are literal characters (GAP-10). It also assumes no seed title or author contains '_'.
Assumes per-field matching: the whole query must be in the title or in the author (GAP-11).
Assumes a no-match search returns 200 with the text 'No books found' (GAP-04).
Assumes the card layout and title-ascending order (GAP-04, GAP-08).
Assumes the seed data has 50 books and '1984' comes first (GAP-08).
Assumes whitespace-only and missing q behave like an empty q (GAP-06, GAP-03).
Assumes the limit is 100 and exactly 100 is accepted (GAP-05).

Assumes a 400 status, the

fragment, the exact message, and no echo of the input (GAP-07).
Assumes length is measured after trimming (GAP-05).
Assumes the limit counts Unicode characters, not bytes (GAP-05).
Assumes repeated or nested q is rejected with 400 and the single-text message (GAP-03). The briefing marks this low confidence.
Assumes injection-style text is plain text and that the seed contains the two titles with an apostrophe (GAP-09).
Assumes injection-style text is plain text and never changes data (GAP-09).

left_out.why: Rare. It is not an acceptance criterion and adds only a small check on top of TC-11.

left_out.what: Checking that the bound-value rule is met in the code (no string-built SQL)
left_out.why: This is internal structure. Tests at the entry point can only show its effect, and TC-17 and TC-18 do that.

left_out.what: Search box in the browser: htmx:beforeSwap allowing 400, and the error replacing earlier results
left_out.why: The briefing calls the listener a non-binding hint, and the tests are supertest only, with no browser.

left_out.what: HTML escaping of hostile title or author text
left_out.why: This needs book data that the seed does not contain. Test data setup is outside the briefing, and TC-17 covers escaping with the apostrophe titles.

left_out.what: Separate test for a book matching in both fields appearing once
left_out.why: It is folded into TC-05, which checks the same rule.

left_out.what: Very long input (10,000 characters) or timing
left_out.why: Rare. TC-13 already shows the over-limit rule.

left_out.what: Regression of the existing home page list
left_out.why: The briefing does not say to keep any behaviour unchanged, and it states no relation to this.

left_out.what: JSON endpoint or other HTTP methods
left_out.why: The briefing says there is no JSON endpoint and states nothing else.

notes: AC-06 and AC-07 are about the test suite itself, so they have no tests of their own. AC-05 is shown only through behaviour (TC-17, TC-18, plus TC-08 for literal wildcards). No black-box test can prove the query text never appears inside the SQL text. Relations covered: AC-01 with AC-02 (TC-09), AC-03 with AC-04 (TC-14), AC-03 with AC-02 (TC-10). AC-05 constrains AC-01 and is tested under that constraint (TC-17). Rare tests: 2 of 18 (TC-15, TC-16).
